Donald: It’s okay, Gloria. I was a bit taken aback at first, but I know you meant well. It’s just a lot to process.

Scenario 4:

steps.raw_response:
From Gloria’s perspective:

At first, I only saw what was visible: Donald seemed bored and distracted while serving drinks, and over several events, that pattern made me think he was simply unhappy with his job. That felt like the obvious explanation.

But after our first real conversation, I couldn’t shake the feeling that it went deeper. The way he said the work was “repetitive” didn’t fully explain the heaviness I sensed in him. So I started to wonder if his dissatisfaction at work was really a surface symptom of something more personal going on in his life. My belief shifted from “Donald is unhappy with his job” to “Donald might be dealing with personal issues that are affecting how he feels at work.”

That’s what led me to suggest professional help—not because I assumed something was wrong, but because I genuinely believed his struggle might be bigger than the job itself.
